title: Target restriction preserves the base-change image
statement: With the canonical stalk maps [def-sbc-canonical-base-change-stalk-transitions], for any φ:U→V over T and η∈A(V), r_φ(b_V(η)) belongs to the image of b_U. There are no affine, qcqs, degree or injectivity assumptions.

source.place: Tags 0F07 (restriction square and limit condition) and 09Z1 (higher direct image continuity)

proof.text: Compatibility of base change with transitions gives b_V followed by the target transition equal to the source transition followed by base change. Naturality with respect to the coefficient-composition isomorphism completes the square. Associativity identifies the two structure morphisms; after this identification their base-change maps have the same range. Apply the geometric stalk functor and take the image of η under the source comparison as the preimage.

mathlib_searches.results: Concrete.colimit_rep_eq_zero and ModuleCat.FilteredColimits.M.mk_surjective, M.mk_map, M.mk_eq; abstract criteria only, not the geometric realization. Loogle confirmed Concrete.colimit_rep_eq_zero.

Existing higherDirectImage_limit supplies stalk continuity for higher images, but not source inverse-image/homology identification or target pullback/coefficient identification. Existing target composition and base-change naturality supply the two proved compatibility lemmas. No canonical stalk wrappers or source-image descent/target-zero detection declarations found.
